figure: Figure 6.2 — Latency distribution: the mean hides the tail
issue: The caption promises two visually distinct shaded regions, but only one is rendered. The caption states: 'the light band shades the full SLO-violating region (> 2 s, everything right of the SLO line) and the darker hatched band marks the 5 s straggler cluster inside it.' In the 150 dpi render, the region from the 2 s SLO line out to ~4.5 s shows no fill that is distinguishable from the white plot background; the only visible band is the 4.5–5.5 s straggler cluster (light-pink fill + red diagonal hatching). The figure's central pedagogical device — distinguishing the entire SLO-violating region from the narrow straggler cluster — is therefore not carried by the drawing. A reader (especially in grayscale, where the faint pink would wash to near-white) can only see the hatched cluster and must rely on the floating red text label 'SLO-violating region (> 2 s)' to infer that everything right of the SLO line violates, which is exactly the inference the band was meant to make visually.
evidence: Caption text (quoted above) vs. rendered plot: right of the blue dash-dot SLO line at x=2, the background between gridlines is white through x≈4.5; the hatched band appears only at x≈4.5–5.5. No solid light band spans 2→6 s. The red annotation 'SLO-violating region (> 2 s)' sits at x≈2.5–4 but is text, not a band.
acceptance_test: Rebuild the figure so that a solid light band (a fill clearly different from the white background AND clearly different from the hatched straggler band) spans the full region right of the 2 s SLO line (2 s → 6 s). Verify at 150 dpi and in grayscale that this light band is distinguishable from both the plot background and the hatched 4.5–5.5 s band, so the two-band distinction in the caption is visually self-evident without reading the red text label.
